retained_secondary_improvement.action: A whole-paper review found no originally evaluated computational-performance endpoint that can be surpassed on the same neural-data task. Figures 2-5 report biological effects and associations; the odd/even grid analysis estimates held-half modulation rather than predictive error. Participant behavioral accuracy is ordered but describes the original human cohort, not an author computational method. Replacing those participants with a machine solver changes the population. This conclusion is not restricted to the legacy ripple-model reconstruction. Whole-paper computational analyses assess biological effects, associations and modulation, without an eligible ordered original algorithm-performance endpoint. The odd/even grid procedure refits modulation on its test half and reports beta1; no predictive-loss or known-orientation recovery baseline is supplied. The reported human behavioral accuracy cannot become a machine-solver baseline without changing the scientific population and intervention. The threshold ripple detector is not evaluated against ground-truth event labels, and content-specific replay decoding is discussed as future work; neither provides an original task baseline.
